business_problem: A major Canadian bank needed to unify fragmented capital-markets data spread across dozens of applications and domains so teams could stop duplicating information and start producing trusted analytics and AI-driven insights faster.
solution_summary: The capital-markets division of a major Canadian bank built a unified data hub on MongoDB Enterprise Advanced and MongoDB Atlas to replace siloed data stores spread across 76 applications and 113 data domains. The new architecture uses MongoDB’s flexible document model as the core of a data-mesh strategy so domain teams can own and publish data products while reducing duplication and governance drift. The bank consolidated client, market, transaction, and risk data into one hub, then integrated Databricks for machine learning, visualization, and other analytics workloads. MongoDB’s querying, indexing, replication, and multiregional failover support dashboards, recommender systems, and resilient disaster recovery, while Atlas security features such as SSO SAML and encryption helped satisfy enterprise compliance requirements. By treating MongoDB as the shared operational core, the bank created a faster route to trusted analytics across capital markets.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Provides the initial production data-hub foundation for capital-markets data before workloads migrate to Atlas.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Delivers the managed multiregional cloud database and security features the bank uses for its modernized data platform.

solution_components.name: Databricks
solution_components.role: Consumes data from MongoDB to support machine learning, data visualization, and other advanced analytical use cases.

data_flow: Client, market, transaction, and risk data from dozens of applications are consolidated into a MongoDB-based data hub, queried and indexed for domain teams, then extended into Databricks and BI tooling for dashboards, machine learning, chatbots, and recommender workflows.
business_outcome: The bank modernized its capital-markets data foundation, accelerated integration of new data sources, reduced duplication, and created a resilient platform for analytics and AI initiatives that can move new ideas to market faster.
metrics: The bank’s IT team oversaw 76 applications and 113 data domains in the Capital Markets division.
Tens of millions of records flowed through these disparate systems daily.
The division planned to migrate production workloads from MongoDB Enterprise Advanced to MongoDB Atlas in August 2024.
architecture_clues: The solution uses a data-mesh approach so domain teams can manage data as products.
MongoDB multiregional clusters use replication and failover for resilience and disaster recovery.
SSO SAML integration and encryption were important Atlas features for compliance acceptance.
Databricks is integrated for machine learning, data visualization, and advanced analytics.
evidence_quotes: “We needed to implement a central, flexible, scalable, and resilient home for capital markets data.”
“MongoDB Atlas checked all the boxes and would let us adopt features like SSO SAML integration, encryption, and different support tiers that fit the criticality of our use cases.”
“By extending the data hub to other frameworks, we’ve built strategic dashboards using business intelligence tools.”
“MongoDB has proven to be production ready, resilient, adaptable, scalable, and widely used.”
